risks.how: cancelEvent only cancels bookings and tickets with no refund request, and refunds are refused once the event has started.

risks.how: Keys are generated at startup when unset, the webhook secret has a known compose default, and all DB users have the password local_dev_only.

risks.reference: Redis is on event-service's write path: business transactions evict the cache by calling `Cache.evict` directly, which
risks.how: Cache eviction and cached reads run in the request path with no error handler, so a Redis failure fails the request.

risks.how: publish and cancel call venue-service over HTTP while the event row changes inside the open transaction; the owner reference makes reserve idempotent.

risks.how: ticket.issued carries email, phone and the signed QR token, which notification-service copies into its variables.

risks.reference: Single points of failure in the only deployment: one Kafka node with replication factor 1 and auto-created topics, one
risks.how: One postgres, one redis and one single-node kafka with replication factor 1 are the whole deployment.

risks.reference: The payment provider is an in-process fake that keeps payment state in memory.
risks.how: The fake provider keeps payment behaviour in a ConcurrentHashMap and reports an unknown id as failed after a restart.

risks.reference: Compensation refunds call the provider inside the Kafka consumer's database transaction.
risks.how: The Kafka listener is transactional and calls the refund service, which calls the provider, inside that transaction.

risks.reference: Any EVENT_STAFF user may validate and check in tickets for every event; staff are not tied to events.
risks.how: mayScan lets any EVENT_STAFF scan any event's tickets.

risks.reference: Cancelling an event does not stop bookings still awaiting payment: payment-service never hears of the cancellation,
risks.how: None of the payment, inventory-confirm or booking-confirm steps check the event's cancelled status.

risks.reference: Reminders and cancellation alerts are not withdrawn for bookings that end without tickets: notification-service plans
risks.how: Reminders are planned on booking.created, the switch has no case for failed, expired or refunded bookings, and cancellation alerts go to all seen bookings.

risks.reference: The gateway rate-limits by the TCP peer address and ignores `X-Forwarded-For`, while the frontend's nginx proxies
risks.how: The limiter keys on the peer address while nginx proxies every request to the gateway.

risks.reference: Every service port (8081-8086) is published on the host next to the gateway.
risks.how: Each service publishes its port on the host next to the gateway.

risks.reference: Reschedule alerts cannot fire: event details can change only while an event is a draft, and bookings exist only once
risks.how: Details are locked after draft and bookings need open sales, so rescheduleEvent never has a booking to alert.

risks.how: The only email and SMS senders are conditional on provider 'local'; any other value leaves no bean.

decoys.looksLike: Identity headers like X-User-Id and X-User-Roles could be trusted from the request.
decoys.safeBecause: The gateway's highest-precedence filter removes all six identity headers from every incoming request, and services read identity from the JWT.

decoys.looksLike: The gateway handles CORS by hand and might allow any origin.
decoys.safeBecause: The filter rejects any Origin not in the configured allowed-origins list (default http://localhost:3000) with 403.

decoys.looksLike: event-service sends to Kafka from inside a @Transactional method.
decoys.safeBecause: The relay only sends rows already committed to the outbox table by earlier business transactions, and marks them published afterwards.

decoys.looksLike: No schema migrations: JPA could create the schema.
decoys.safeBecause: Hibernate runs with ddl-auto validate and Flyway applies versioned scripts from db/migration.
